channel.title: Wire — Programming
channel.description: Programming from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
item.description: We are introducing Clef and Clef-flash, open-source decision models hosted on Workers AI for high-speed classification and agentic workflows. (2 sources: cloudflare, hackernews)

item.title: Hanami, Why?: Introductions
item.description: I mentioned in my Hello, world! post that I built this site using Hanami. This site may seem simple on the surface; it is, after all, just a blog. However, the backend is packed with features that help me day to day. (2 sources: lobsters, rubyweekly)

item.title: Git 3.0's upcoming SHA-256 default will be a costly mistake
Article: High Availability Is Not Resilience: Why Cloud Systems Fail When It Matters Most
item.description: A routine TLS 1.3 upgrade silently broke Route 53 health checks, causing a CDN to stop routing traffic to a healthy region while internal dashboards showed nothing wrong. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: How to make a text box: A crash course in Unicode and OpenType - Jimmy Lefevre, BSC 2026
Lists that keep track of their reversal
item.description: Summary of a small discussion on how to track, at type level, whether a list is constructed forwards or backwards. It remains to be seen whether this will be useful in everyday life, but the proposal is driven by a specific issue. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: StreetComplete on iOS is now in public beta
item.description: This ticket is something like the master ticket to coordinate development on an iOS port of StreetComplete. It replaces #1892 which also included a lot of discussion and research / observation work. TLDR: Have a look at the Project Board... (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: A brief history of the Bloomberg terminal
item.description: It gave Wall Street traders and analysts an unprecedented window on global markets (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Google breaks promise to provide 10 years of updates to Chromebooks
Cops Can Bypass iPhone's Automatic Reboot to Get into Locked Phones
item.description: Magent Forensics, the owner of the GrayKey phone unlocking tool, says it can bypass an iPhone rebooting feature that was locking cops out. (1 source: hackernews)
